services.name: Cloud Storage

persistence.restartBehavior: Survives process and container restart while the LocalCloud volume is retained
recoveryLimitations: No production durability or replication semantics.

limitations: [partial] Bucket policy APIs use gateway 5380/TLS 5381. Object authorization is enforced at both direct listeners and the gateway when IAM mode requires it.
[partial] gcp-live uses caller-token Google permission checks with no fallback. Real-Google and object-conditional grant qualification remain pending; unsupported remote grants fail closed.
[partial] Open mode deliberately permits known-bucket access; project listing uses authoritative ownership and is not an open-mode tenant security boundary.
[partial] Notification delivery uses precreated local Pub/Sub topics. Persisted messages retry after failure/restart; ordering and transactional object/outbox crash atomicity are not promised.

[unsupported] Object Versioning and OBJECT_ARCHIVE notifications are implemented on the filesystem backend but have no image or platform evidence yet: no image has been built with them and the StoragePlatformTest versioning cases have not been executed. Finalize, metadata-update and delete delivery are live-container qualified.

[partial] In a bucket with versioning.enabled, replacing, deleting or moving a live object keeps it as a noncurrent generation, and get, download, a rewrite or copy source and delete take a generation; a delete with a generation is permanent, also for the live object. versions=true lists every generation, and a bucket that still holds one is not deleted (409). Objects have a real metageneration that patch and update raise, and ifMetagenerationMatch and ifMetagenerationNotMatch are checked against it. Limits: compose ignores sourceObjects[].generation and reads the live objects; objectAccessControls insert, update and delete still answer 501 and so change neither the ACL nor the metageneration; a patch does not move the updated time; each noncurrent generation is a file directly in the storage root, which the bucket list and a versioned listing read, and the cost of many generations has not been measured; exports, checkpoints and seed files carry the versioning setting but no noncurrent generation.

[partial] HMAC supports local project-ID-scoped service-account identities. Project-number aliases and default-compute identities are not resolved; real-Google gcp-live impersonation is not qualified. Secrets are excluded from project YAML exports; encrypted key state is retained in full filesystem snapshots.

[prod_only] Object lifecycle scheduling and retention enforcement are excluded from developer completeness. The configuration is stored and returned, but lifecycle rules do not run, and holds and retention do not block an overwrite or a delete.

[partial] Objects keep temporaryHold, eventBasedHold (a new object in a bucket with defaultEventBasedHold starts held) and kmsKeyName, and return them. The key name is returned as given, without a cryptoKeyVersions suffix. Nothing is encrypted, and a bucket's default key is not applied to its objects. A copy or rewrite destination does not inherit holds or the key from its source.
[unsupported] Managed-folder APIs are not implemented.

[unsupported] Requests the filesystem backend cannot serve are refused with HTTP 501 notImplemented instead of 500: objectAccessControls insert, update and delete (objects.patch with an acl field works), and object names its path-per-name layout cannot hold. Those are content in an object whose name ends in /, an object named like a directory that holds objects (a beside a/b), an object or folder placeholder under an object, a name that ends in //, and a move of a folder placeholder. The Go client retries every 5xx, so it retries these too.

[partial] objects.list counts items and prefixes together against maxResults, and nextPageToken is opaque; a pageToken that no listing returned answers 400. Without maxResults, or with 0, the whole listing comes in one page, where Cloud Storage pages at 1000 entries. softDeleted=true returns an empty list, because nothing is soft-deleted here; it answers 400 together with versions=true and 400 invalidArgument for a bucket whose soft delete policy has a retention duration of zero. An object whose name ends in / is stored as a zero-byte folder placeholder and returned with includeTrailingDelimiter=true. Deleting a bucket that still holds objects answers 409, not 412.

[unsupported] XML multipart upload (initiate, upload part, complete, abort, list) is refused with 501, which affects S3-style large uploads through HMAC keys. There is no gRPC Storage API; the legacy storage.v1 gRPC service is no longer served.

[partial] Resumable uploads follow Google's protocol for status queries, persisted ranges, repeated chunks and gaps, but a status query after the upload completed answers 404, and the header-based X-Goog-Upload-Command protocol is not implemented. Object reads honour ifGenerationMatch, ifGenerationNotMatch, ifMetagenerationMatch and ifMetagenerationNotMatch as query parameters, not as x-goog-if-* headers. Rewrite and copy apply storageClass and customTime from the request body; other body fields are merged with the source object's metadata and the source ACL is copied.

[partial] Bucket metadata: buckets.insert, patch, update (PUT) and get keep labels, uniform bucket-level access, public access prevention, location, storage class and metageneration, and patch/update honor ifMetagenerationMatch. Lifecycle, CORS, website, logging, retention policy, object retention, soft-delete, hierarchical-namespace, RPO, encryption, billing, Autoclass, custom placement and IP filter fields are stored and returned as given but have no effect; patch merges them and a null clears one. The server sets retentionPolicy.effectiveTime and the Autoclass times. buckets.lockRetentionPolicy is not served, and a bucket acl sent in patch or update and defaultObjectAcl are still dropped. Export and project checkpoints carry only a bucket's name, location and versioning setting and each live object's bytes and content type, so a restore loses the other metadata and every noncurrent generation. projectNumber is always 0, so import buckets into Terraform as project/bucket; a bare-name import falls back to the provider's default project.

[partial] Path-style HMAC XML requests accept localhost and loopback IPs with discovered Docker ports. Virtual-host requests use the configured public hostname (localhost); signed Host headers must not be rewritten after signing.

[partial] LocalCloud's own Storage work (seed, reset, remote-sync import and manifest cleanup, project checkpoints and migration fixtures) runs as LocalCloud with a process-local internal credential, so strict and gcp-live policies do not block it; sync refuses a bucket another local project owns. Console browse, mutation and export keep the caller's identity, and Workflows Storage connectors run as the workflow's service account (the Workflows service agent when none is set). Only the Storage section of an export is authorized as its caller; GET /export is an admin endpoint outside the gateway's IAM check, its other sections are read for whoever calls it, and a Storage listing the caller may not make leaves gcs out of the export and names it under unreadable_services. A reset whose Storage listing or deletes the running emulator rejects reports partial_failure, and a failed sync-manifest cleanup keeps the manifest; an unreachable emulator is still treated as having nothing to reset. A project reset deletes every generation of every object, page by page, before it deletes the bucket, and reports a generation it cannot delete, with its number, as a partial failure that keeps the bucket. A seed accepts versioning: true (or versioning.enabled) for a bucket it creates and uploads a name ending in / as a folder placeholder; an export writes versioning: true for a versioned bucket. A seeded bucket reads location and storage_class, and each of its objects key with content (text) or contentBase64 and an optional contentType; the seed schema (localcloud_get_seed_schema) publishes these keys, and an export writes key, contentBase64 and contentType. An object entry without key is not created, with a warning in the server log, while its bucket is. Console browse, export and the migration capture follow nextPageToken to the last page. A sync names an object local Storage cannot hold in its result and copies the rest, and deleting a sync manifest deletes every generation under its prefix.

[partial] Local live-container HTTP qualification includes multipart uploads, admin caller propagation, strict signed IAM, notification recovery and reset. These fixes require a rebuilt image; trusted release-image and full LocalCloud TLS qualification remain pending.

operations.label: buckets.create/list/delete
limitations: Core bucket lifecycle through the local HTTP emulator. Bucket get, patch and update (PUT) keep the metadata listed in the limitations.

operations.label: objects.upload/download/list/delete
limitations: Core object lifecycle through the local HTTP emulator.

operations.label: buckets.getIamPolicy/setIamPolicy/testIamPermissions
limitations: Gateway policy API uses project-owned local policies. Strict checks shared IAM permissions; gcp-live reads Google policy/permissions with caller credentials and rejects policy writes. Direct object requests have a separate shared authorization boundary.

operations.label: mode-aware object data-plane authorization
limitations: Both direct HTTP/TLS and gateway traffic use the Go request boundary. Open bypasses, permissive evaluates/logs, strict checks project/bucket/object policies, and gcp-live tests Google permissions without fallback. Storage Object Creator grants creation only; reading, listing, overwriting and copying/composing unreadable source objects require additional permissions. Unavailable authorization fails closed.

operations.label: notificationConfigs.create/list/delete and Pub/Sub event delivery
limitations: Existing local topics receive filtered finalize, metadata-update and delete events in the filesystem-backed container. Configuration and pending messages survive restart; failed delivery retries, and full Storage reset clears both. Archive events need a versioned bucket; the server raises OBJECT_ARCHIVE there and OBJECT_DELETE for a generation deleted by number, but their delivery to local Pub/Sub from the container is not qualified. Use --skip-topic-setup with precreated local Pub/Sub topics.

operations.label: HMAC key management and XML signature authentication
limitations: Project-scoped key CRUD, encrypted persistence, quota, etags and revocation; Google/AWS V2/V4 XML header, URL and form authentication. Strict IAM uses the verified service-account principal; gcp-live requires server ADC impersonation and fails closed. Local service-account identities are logical principals, not an IAM service-account CRUD registry.

operations.label: Object Lifecycle Management and retention enforcement
limitations: Production governance and automatic lifecycle scheduling are outside the developer support contract by product decision. Lifecycle, retention and hold configuration is stored and returned but never enforced.

operations.label: managed folders
limitations: Managed-folder APIs are outside the current implementation.

operations.label: persistent bucket versioning and OBJECT_ARCHIVE notifications
limitations: Implemented in the Storage emulator patch for the filesystem backend the container runs. versioning.enabled is stored on bucket insert, patch and update and survives a restart; replacing, deleting or moving a live object keeps it as a noncurrent generation; get, download, a rewrite or copy source and delete address a generation by number, and a delete with a generation is permanent; versions=true lists live and noncurrent generations by name and generation; a bucket that still holds a generation is not deleted (409); and the server raises OBJECT_ARCHIVE for a replaced or deleted live object. The status is unchanged because the only evidence is the patched emulator's Go tests on the memory and filesystem backends (TestObjectVersioning, TestServerObjectVersions, TestServerObjectVersionEvents, TestServerObjectMetageneration) and LocalCloud component tests against an in-JVM Storage fake; no image has been built with it and the StoragePlatformTest versioning cases have not been executed.

services.name: Pub/Sub

persistence.restartBehavior: Topics, subscriptions, and queued messages persist in PostgreSQL. Delivery workers and active connections restart; qualify the exact replay and redelivery workflow.
recoveryLimitations: A mounted volume does not provide production delivery, replication, or recovery guarantees; qualify the assembled image.

limitations: Exactly-once delivery, message ordering (enableMessageOrdering), export subscriptions and transforms remain unsupported, as do topic kmsKeyName and ingestionDataSourceSettings. A request that sets one of them is refused with UNIMPLEMENTED (HTTP 501). The x-goog-version push attribute accepts v1 and v1beta2; v1beta1 is refused the same way.

Subscription expirationPolicy is stored and returned but, by design for development use, not enforced, so no subscription expires locally. A subscription created without a policy returns none, where Google returns a 31-day default. A finite TTL must be at least one day and at least the message retention. Topic messageStoragePolicy is stored and returned with no local effect, and region names are not checked.

Unwrapped pushes (pushConfig.noWrapper) carry no delivery-attempt header. With writeMetadata, a message attribute that cannot be an HTTP header is left out and the message is still pushed. Every read of a push subscription returns pushConfig.attributes with x-goog-version.

Deleting a topic keeps its subscriptions, pointed at _deleted-topic_, with their backlog, as Google does. A deleted topic can be recreated at once, where Google may answer an error for a brief period. Snapshots of a deleted topic are kept until they expire, and a subscription cannot be created on _deleted-topic_.

Authenticated push tokens are signed by the LocalCloud issuer (/identity/status, keys at /oauth2/v3/certs), not https://accounts.google.com; receivers must trust the local JWKS. Revoking the Pub/Sub service agent's token-creator role is not modeled.
Retry dispatch and retention cleanup are approximate local schedules; this does not reproduce Google production scale, availability or service-agent IAM.
Schema definitions must be self-contained; imported protobuf types are unsupported, matching the Pub/Sub schema restriction.

Stored Pub/Sub IAM policies can be read and evaluated through IAM APIs, but no Pub/Sub operation enforces those resource bindings. Strict mode and successful testIamPermissions do not establish Pub/Sub data-plane authorization. The gateway checks only that the caller is credentialed and allowed on the path, and the direct listener (5383, where PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST points) accepts unauthenticated calls in every mode.

A seed entry for a topic or subscription is the REST resource (name, topic and a dead-letter topic may be IDs), validated and saved as CreateTopic and CreateSubscription do. The Pub/Sub section of a seed is applied as a whole and creates only what is absent, so a topic or subscription that exists is left unchanged. A value the API refuses, or a key the seed does not read, fails the section with the API's message (HTTP 500 on /import) and nothing in it is written. Seeded messages are published only to a topic the seed creates. In strict and gcp-live modes the caller of the seed needs iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on a push subscription's oidcToken account, and a seed applied without a caller (an automatic sample, or the restore a runtime-migration run makes) is anonymous and refused when it holds such a subscription. A checkpoint restore with replace, a reset to the seed baseline and a migration restore check the Pub/Sub section before they clear anything, so a refused one leaves the project's topics and subscriptions as they were; a subscription to another project's topic that is missing is refused only after the reset. In strict and gcp-live modes a runtime-migration run on a project that holds an OIDC push subscription therefore ends FAILED (Unable to restore equivalent emulator state) before it clears anything.

An export, a project checkpoint and a migration capture write each topic and subscription with the fields the API returns, in the form a seed reads, so export, reset and import restore the configuration, including a subscription on _deleted-topic_. Messages, snapshots, schemas and a topic's schemaSettings are not exported, and a dead-letter policy whose topic in the same project no longer exists is left out with a warning in the server log. The section is read from the Pub/Sub store without an API request, so it is the same in open, permissive, strict and gcp-live modes and is not counted as usage. GET /export is an admin endpoint outside the gateway's IAM check, so whoever can call the admin API receives a project's topic and subscription configuration in every mode; no Pub/Sub permission is evaluated for it. Seed and export parity is component-tested (SeedExportParityComponentTest) and has not run on an image.

operations.label: topics.create/get/list/update/delete
limitations: A seed entry for a topic is the same REST resource, validated and saved as topics.create does, and an export writes every field the API returns except schemaSettings (SeedExportParityComponentTest; component evidence, not run on an image).

operations.label: subscriptions.create/get/list/update/delete/modifyPushConfig
limitations: A seed entry for a subscription is the same REST resource, validated and saved as subscriptions.create does (pushConfig, deadLetterPolicy, retryPolicy, filter, retention and expirationPolicy included), and an export writes the fields the API returns; the limitations name what an export leaves out (SeedExportParityComponentTest; component evidence, not run on an image).

operations.label: publish/pull/ack/modifyAckDeadline
limitations: StreamingPull protocol version one receives empty keepalive responses independently of message flow-control capacity. Protocol version is negotiated only on the initial request.

operations.label: subscription filters, dead-letter forwarding, retry policies
limitations: Strict immutable attribute filters and shared pull/StreamingPull/push retry scheduling with dead-letter source metadata.

operations.label: retention, snapshot CRUD, timestamp and snapshot seek
limitations: Durable protected history and atomic replay rotate acknowledgment IDs. Mutation transactions serialize across processes.

operations.label: schema and revision lifecycle, validation, publish enforcement
limitations: Avro 1.11 and proto2/proto3, JSON/binary, revision ranges, and atomic publish batches.

operations.label: PushConfig oidcToken on create/update/modifyPushConfig, signed push delivery
limitations: google.pubsub.v1 PushConfig.OidcToken (proto-google-cloud-pubsub-v1 1.157.0) is accepted over REST and gRPC, persisted in the subscription and returned on readback. Each push attempt sends one Authorization: Bearer ID token from the LocalCloud issuer for serviceAccountEmail, with the email claim and the configured audience or, when empty, the exact push endpoint URL. In enforcing IAM modes (strict, gcp-live), setting it requires iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the account. The Pub/Sub service agent's token-creator grant is modeled as Google's default; revoking it is not. If no token can be minted (account missing, disabled or identity not ready), the message is not sent and follows the normal NACK, retry and dead-letter path, and LocalCloud logs IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE:<reason>; sibling subscriptions on the topic are unaffected. Google requires an explicit token-creator grant to the service agent only for projects that enabled Pub/Sub on or before 2021-04-08, so a missing agent grant cannot occur locally. A non-2xx endpoint response is a NACK: the message is redelivered with a freshly minted token. A seed that holds a subscription with oidcToken is authorized the same way, for the caller of the seed (SeedExportParityComponentTest). The actAs check is component-tested in strict mode. Partial until the packaged-image receipt test has run against a candidate image.

operations.label: push payload unwrapping (noWrapper), pubsubWrapper and the x-goog-version push attribute
limitations: An unwrapped push sends the message data byte for byte; with writeMetadata it adds the x-goog-pubsub subscription-name, message-id, publish-time and ordering-key headers and one header per message attribute. Create, get, list, update and modifyPushConfig round-trip the fields on gRPC and REST and across a restart. Component-tested; partial until the packaged-image push case has run on a candidate image.

operations.label: subscription expirationPolicy and topic messageStoragePolicy
limitations: Both are validated, stored and returned on gRPC and REST and across a restart. expirationPolicy is not enforced and messageStoragePolicy has no local effect.

operations.label: exactly-once delivery, message ordering, export subscriptions and transforms
limitations: Outside the reviewed implementation scope; unsupported fields fail explicitly.

services.name: Firestore

persistence.backingStore: External emulator exports and checkpoint metadata beneath the mounted LocalCloud data root
persistence.restartBehavior: Historical isolated clean-restart evidence restored document contents but changed timestamps. Qualify recovery in the exact assembled image.
recoveryLimitations: Checkpoints and seed registration do not establish timestamp, precondition, listener, or transaction fidelity.

limitations: Firestore is supported locally but disabled by default to save system resources. Enable via localcloud start --services firestore or services.enabled in configuration.

All three Firestore platform test classes (FirestorePlatformTest, FirestoreSeedPlatformTest and FirestoreRecoveryPlatformTest) are tagged pending-service and listed in ci/deferred_tests.json, so the platform suite runs them only when Firestore is enabled for the run explicitly. The latest runs are from 2026-10-13 on the published 0.1.6 image, each class alone. On the image as published FirestorePlatformTest and the graceful restart case passed, the case that disables Firestore failed and the seed case found no sample on a loaded host. With the current server JAR mounted over that image all five cases passed, which is not exact-image evidence. No image built from the current source has run them.

In images up to 0.1.6, disabling or restarting Firestore through the admin API answers 500 supervisor_stop_failed when its graceful stop takes longer than five seconds, and leaves the service enabled with its emulator stopped; enable it again or restart the container. The five-second limit applied to the stop of every supervised emulator and was observed for Firestore. In the current source a stop is given 100 seconds.

The default sample is requested once, when the gateway backend becomes healthy. A service that is enabled but not healthy at that moment gets its sample when it becomes healthy, within three minutes, and POST /seed/default names it under deferred_until_healthy; its sample stays pending for the next container start or enable call when the service is disabled, fails or does not become healthy in time. In images up to 0.1.6 nothing applied the sample when the service became healthy, and on a host where the backend needed more than about a minute to start no sample was requested at all, without a log line; this affected every service's sample. The current source waits up to 15 minutes for the backend and logs when it gives up. POST /seed/default requests the samples again.
Google-operated multi-region replication and production scale are cloud-only.

Composite-index enforcement, transaction concurrency, listeners and transforms require exact-artifact qualification. Security Rules evaluation and Firestore-trigger delivery remain unqualified local capabilities.

Documents are written to the checkpoint only when the Firestore process stops gracefully, on SIGTERM, SIGINT or the emulator's shutdown endpoint; there is no periodic checkpoint. A kill, a crash, or a stop whose export does not finish within Supervisor's 90-second wait loses every write made since the previous checkpoint.
The emulator is started without a Security Rules file and LocalCloud has no setting that supplies one, so an application's rules are not loaded.

Datastore API calls, such as POST /v1/projects/{project}:lookup, are refused by the Firestore listener with HTTP 400 (Database mode not set to Datastore Mode) because the emulator runs in native mode. LocalCloud starts no Datastore-mode instance.

limitations: Firestore document CRUD operations supported locally on port 5384.

services.name: Bigtable

persistence.restartBehavior: LocalCloud Docker is intended to retain PostgreSQL-backed service data while the mounted /var/lib/localcloud volume is retained
recoveryLimitations: The machine-local cached artifact can use PostgreSQL or SQLite, but the LocalCloud Docker product is configured for PostgreSQL.
Dependency identity, restart recovery, and the assembled LocalCloud image remain release-unverified.

limitations: The pinned little_bigtable dd5f9e7 (v0.5.0) passes its dependency test suite, and its executable ledger covers all 89 registered RPCs. That evidence is for the dependency source, not LocalCloud. It ran on SQLite rather than LocalCloud's PostgreSQL backend and skipped the pinned cbt test. The 2026-10-05 UTC arm64 candidate (sha256:2bd0813e574ddf6af1bfd9be6f3b318e6290117b4c5fc1142d651de5d274b754) embeds this revision and completed platform testing with two failing Bigtable cases (project deletion and backup listing). The LocalCloud fixes for both pass BigtablePlatformTest with a source JAR over that image; exact-image and full LocalCloud Bigtable qualification remain open.
IAM policies persist but are not enforced. TestIamPermissions grants every requested permission because the emulator is unauthenticated; the direct gRPC listener also bypasses gateway IAM.

Change streams use one partition with no split or merge. last_scanned_row_key is not emitted, logical views do not support view parameters, query statistics are not recorded, and google.cloud.location.Locations is not served.
HLL++ aggregate sketch bytes and multi-column materialized-view row keys use emulator-specific encodings that are not byte-compatible with production.

Legacy table snapshot RPCs (SnapshotTable, GetSnapshot, ListSnapshots, DeleteSnapshot, CreateTableFromSnapshot) return Unimplemented; they are a deprecated private-alpha API. Use backups for data protection.

The Console REST admin facade ignores emulator errors on row writes and deletes and on app-profile and view routes, then reports success from local placeholder state. Instance PATCH/PUT and table PATCH answer locally without reaching the emulator, and logical and materialized view updates drop their update masks. Verify through the native API when a result must reflect emulator validation.

assembledDefault.limitation: Default enablement follows the current runtime catalog and remains subject to license-tier gates.

operations.label: instances/tables/families
limitations: The pinned little_bigtable dd5f9e7 (v0.5.0) emulates instance, cluster, app-profile, table and schema-bundle administration as validated metadata (ID and field rules, response views, update masks, pagination, deletion protection, soft delete and 7-day undelete, atomic column-family changes, initial splits, row key schema) with a durable long-running-operation registry. Cluster nodes and autoscaling settings are stored without capacity effects. Dependency conformance tests pass; LocalCloud image qualification of this revision is pending.

operations.label: row mutations and reads
limitations: dd5f9e7 validates every mutation before applying any (single-row atomicity), reports real per-entry MutateRows codes, honors idempotency tokens and aggregate (Sum/Min/Max, HLL++) families, implements every RowFilter including Interleave duplicates, Sink (cells bypass subsequent filters; invalid inside Condition) and ValueBitmask, chunks ReadRows like production with request stats, samples SampleRowKeys within row ranges, enforces authorized-view, materialized-view and app-profile targets, and serves the OpenTable/OpenAuthorizedView/OpenMaterializedView session protocol. last_scanned_row_key is not emitted. Sink output and rejection inside Condition have named dependency conformance tests; a dedicated LocalCloud Sink platform scenario is pending. Dependency conformance tests pass; LocalCloud image qualification is pending.

operations.label: cbt CLI compatibility
limitations:
Set BIGTABLE_EMULATOR_HOST and pass -project to cbt unless the project is already configured in .cbtrc or gcloud. GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT alone does not select the cbt project. Table commands also require -instance. Clear stored -admin-endpoint and -data-endpoint overrides when relying on the emulator variable. A non-secret -access-token=localcloud can avoid credential discovery for local plaintext use; it is optional for the tested cbt version. It is not a Google credential.
Arbitrary project and instance IDs are accepted on-demand without pre-registration, matching Google Cloud SDK CBT emulator behavior.
The gRPC data plane accepts requests without an authorization header or credential provider.
Instance CRUD (create/list/get/delete instance) is supported via gRPC.
Table and row operations work as expected.
Not re-run against little_bigtable dd5f9e7: its pinned cbt conformance test was skipped because cbt was not installed, so this rests on earlier evidence until the LocalCloud image is qualified.

operations.label: localcloud console data browser
limitations:
REST endpoints for instance/table/row CRUD exposed via BigtableAdminService:
- GET  /.../tables/{table}/rows — browse rows
- POST /.../tables/{table}/rows — write cells
- DELETE /.../tables/{table}/rows/{rowKey} — delete row
SDK and console share the same PostgreSQL-backed emulator state.
Instance, table and backup routes forward to the emulator and return its errors with the Google API HTTP mapping (FAILED_PRECONDITION as 400, for example). Row writes and deletes, app-profile and view routes still ignore emulator errors and report success from local placeholder state, and instance PATCH/PUT and table PATCH answer locally without reaching the emulator, so a rejected request on those routes can appear to succeed.

operations.label: data survives emulator restart

limitations: Task and queue OAuth/OIDC credentials are minted by the LocalCloud issuer, not Google, and verify only against LocalCloud's JWKS. A queue httpTarget credential overrides task credentials and every task Authorization header; at queue level both the service account and the audience/scope are required. OIDC audience defaults to the URL the request is sent to, after queue overrides, and OAuth scope to cloud-platform. Each attempt mints through the delivery token cache; when no token can be minted (for example, a disabled or deleted account) the request is not sent and the attempt records IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE:<reason> with normal retry semantics. Strict and gcp-live modes require iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the account when a task or queue is configured; the account is not checked against the queue's project. Redirect responses are not followed.
App Engine delivery and logging sampling are rejected as unsupported rather than silently stored.

The /v2beta3 surface is REST only; there is no v2beta3 gRPC. Pull queues (type PULL and Task.pullMessage), Queue.taskTtl, tombstoneTtl and appEngineHttpQueue, readMask and Queue.stats, the queues.list filter, tasks.batchCreate and tasks.batchDelete answer 501 there, and taskTtl, tombstoneTtl and stats are not returned. Locations, cmekConfig and operations are served on neither version.
BufferTask is served on /v2 and /v2beta3, accepts POST only, and answers FAILED_PRECONDITION when the queue has no httpTarget host. The X-CloudTasks-TaskRetryReason header is not sent.

Seed, export and project checkpoints carry a queue's settings and its REST httpTarget (uriOverride, httpMethod, headerOverrides and the oidcToken or oauthToken member, which names an account and an audience or scope and never holds a token); the seed-only httpTargetUri and httpTargetMethod keys still work. Tasks are not exported, so a restore brings back queues without their tasks, and a seed leaves a queue that exists unchanged. A seeded httpTarget is checked and authorized as CreateQueue does. A queue whose target is refused is not created and the other queues are seeded; /seed, /import and a checkpoint restore still succeed and report it only as a warning in the server log, while /reseed reports the service as failed. In strict and gcp-live modes the caller of the seed needs iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the queue credential's account, so a checkpoint restore with replace by a caller without it clears that queue and does not bring it back. Component-tested (SeedExportParityComponentTest), not run on an image.

No FIFO, exactly-once, dead-letter queue, transactional cancellation, adaptive Google throttling or production throughput guarantees. By default a removed task ID can be reused at once; Google reserves it for up to 24 hours. Setting task_name_reuse_window_seconds (0 to 777600, default 0) makes a create with the ID of a task that was deleted, completed, exhausted or purged within that window answer ALREADY_EXISTS; deleting a queue releases its reserved IDs, and Google's queue-name reuse delay is not implemented. Unlimited retry settings have no automatic task-retention expiry.

HTTP attempt deadlines are durations from 15 to 1800 seconds (default 600). Failed attempts use configured fractional backoff; finite attempt and duration bounds must both be exhausted. A zero duration leaves only the attempt limit; -1 attempts is unlimited.

Local activity retains completed attempt metadata for seven days, with no request URL, headers, payload or response body archive. Interrupted or unpersisted outcomes may remain unknown. Successful/terminal tasks leave the active queue; absence alone is not success.

Pending and interrupted in-flight tasks recover after restart with possible redelivery. Pause, purge and deletion do not cancel requests already in flight. Never replay an ambiguous create or run request automatically.

BASIC omits payload, headers and the OAuth/OIDC configuration; FULL requires cloudtasks.tasks.fullView in enforcing IAM modes. Queue/task operations evaluate stored allow policies in strict and gcp-live modes; open/permissive modes do not enforce them.

It never clears another service. When one of the five cannot be captured, the run ends FAILED with verdict INFRA_ERROR and the finding STATE_CAPTURE_INCOMPLETE naming it, before any reset, fixture or workload. The restore is only as complete as each export section; see those services. A BigQuery read that fails during the state comparison after a case raises the finding STATE_CAPTURE_FAILED; in images up to 0.1.6 it counted as no datasets, no tables or an empty table. IAM Credentials tokens are signed by this runtime's issuer. Receivers must trust the local issuer and JWKS; Google-only verifiers that hardcode Google certificates reject them by design. A disabled or deleted account stops LocalCloud's own verification immediately; an external receiver sees revocation only at token expiry. Disabling or deleting an account key stops its JWT-bearer exchanges, self-signed JWT access and publication immediately, but tokens already issued through that key are not tied to it and stay valid, in LocalCloud and at external receivers, until they expire.

Only Services (create, get, list, update, delete) and Revisions (get, list) are implemented. CreateJob and RunJob answer UNIMPLEMENTED with LocalCloud's unsupported-operation message; GetJob, ListJobs, UpdateJob, DeleteJob and DeleteRevision answer gRPC's default UNIMPLEMENTED; Executions, Tasks, worker pools and every other Cloud Run service are not registered.

A revision is READY, and its operation done, once its startup probe passes. Without a startupProbe that is a TCP connection to the container port, retried for up to 240 seconds; with one it is the configured tcpSocket or httpGet probe within initialDelaySeconds plus failureThreshold times periodSeconds. LocalCloud retries every 250 ms (TCP) or every second (HTTP) inside that window, so a revision is READY as soon as its container listens. healthCheckDisabled skips the probe. Where the port cannot be probed (a relay image without bash, or a LocalCloud container outside the runtime network) readiness falls back to Docker reporting the container running, with a warning in the log.

Service.uri points at a Docker-assigned host port on localhost that belongs to the serving revision's container, so it changes every time an update promotes a new revision and again when a restart relaunches the service. It is empty while no container serves the service. Read uri again after each UpdateService and after a restart.

When Cloud Run starts, a stored service whose container still runs keeps serving at its URI. One whose container is gone is RESTORING while a background thread relaunches its serving revision with the template it was deployed with, creating no revision or generation, and UNAVAILABLE with the reason when that fails or Docker cannot be reached. Cloud Run starts and answers its API without Docker; deployments then fail with the reason. These runtime states are LocalCloud's own; /browse/cloudrun reports them as runtimeState and runtimeMessage.

The gateway proxy /run/invoke/{location}/{project}/{service} reaches the serving revision where the gateway can reach it and streams the response as the application writes it; the request body is read whole. It answers 504 when no response starts within the revision's timeout (template.timeout, 300 seconds by default) and cuts off a response still streaming then, 502 when the application cannot be reached and 503 when the service has no running container. The Cloud Functions trigger path, which also reaches a function backed by a Cloud Run service, still reads the whole response and answers 502 after 15 seconds.
Local domain mappings and host/revision routing are software gaps. Google Front End and production managed routing/TLS guarantees are production-only.

Secret Manager-backed environment variables (v2 env[].valueSource.secretKeyRef, Knative v1 env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef) are not resolved and are rejected with UNIMPLEMENTED (HTTP 501 on v1) instead of being dropped; set literal values.

v2 Service.template reports the serving (latest ready) revision's template, so after a failed update it is not the failed desired template. A deployment reports CONDITION_RECONCILING from admission, never CONDITION_PENDING. A failed create releases the service instead of keeping a failed Service. Revisions report only the Ready condition; uid and etag are not reported.

limitations: Service/revision metadata and Docker create/update execution exist, with launch-failure rollback tests; broader serving/routing semantics remain partial. A create reserves the service name (a duplicate gets ALREADY_EXISTS), one deployment runs per service at a time, and a failed first launch releases the name instead of keeping a failed Service resource. Ingress follows the IAM mode - open admits anonymous calls, permissive verifies and logs, strict and gcp-live require a local ID token whose aud is the uri or a customAudiences entry (401 otherwise, including access tokens) and run.routes.invoke on the service (403). X-Serverless-Authorization, when present, is the only checked credential and reaches the container without its signature. A Cloud Functions invocation of a function backed by the service is checked at the gateway (cloudfunctions functions.metadata) and reaches the relay with a one-time gateway grant, so the caller's own token reaches the container unchanged. UpdateService and Knative replace take the container's env as a whole (a container without env clears it; an update naming no container keeps the serving revision's env, as for its image and port). As in Cloud Run, the four contract names, empty names, names containing '=' or starting with X_GOOGLE_, names or values over 32768 characters or bytes and more than 1000 variables get INVALID_ARGUMENT (HTTP 400 on v1) before anything is reserved. With a workload identity relay, GCE_METADATA_HOST, GCE_METADATA_IP and LOCALCLOUD_RELAY_CAPABILITY are also refused because the relay supplies them (a LocalCloud restriction; Cloud Run does not reserve them). Each revision declares one ADC source on its workload binding - the relay's local metadata (the default), the operator's real credential bridge (gcp_credentials.source adc or service-account, its file mounted read-only at /credentials/gcp.json with GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, and GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT set to its project), or the template's own GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, kept unchanged. A template GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS while the bridge is selected is a conflict, and create and update (v2 and Knative v1) get INVALID_ARGUMENT before anything is reserved or launched. GET /browse/cloudrun reports each service's identity.serviceAccount and identity.credentialSource (local, bridge or user). Service and Revision report deployment status from stored revisions, identically over gRPC and REST. A create or update records its revision when admitted and advances generation; each revision settles READY once its startup probe passes, or FAILED when its launch or probe fails or a restart interrupts its deployment. latestCreatedRevision and latestReadyRevision are full revision names, observedGeneration is the serving revision's generation, and reconciling is true while the latest revision deploys. The Ready terminalCondition and ConfigurationsReady are CONDITION_RECONCILING meanwhile, then CONDITION_SUCCEEDED, or CONDITION_FAILED with reason REVISION_FAILED and the launch error, while the last ready revision keeps serving (RoutesReady). traffic and trafficStatuses report 100 percent TRAFFIC_TARGET_ALLOCATION_TYPE_LATEST once a revision serves. A failed revision's number is not reused. Each Revision reports service, generation 1, observedGeneration 1 once settled, reconciling, a Ready condition and its container port. Knative v1 status (latestCreatedRevisionName, latestReadyRevisionName, observedGeneration, Ready/ConfigurationsReady/RoutesReady with RevisionFailed, traffic) and /browse/cloudrun (latestReadyRevision, latestCreatedRevision, latestCreatedState, reconciling; per revision state and serving) report the same status. Every Service and template field a request sets is applied, stored or refused, the same on v2 and Knative v1, which converts to the v2 Service. Applied to the revision container are command, args, workingDir, resources.limits cpu and memory, startupProbe (tcpSocket or httpGet) and healthCheckDisabled; stored and returned without an effect are template scaling, maxInstanceRequestConcurrency, timeout, executionEnvironment, labels, annotations, the container name, cpuIdle and startupCpuBoost and the Service fields Terraform and gcloud send; the limitations list what is refused. When Cloud Run starts, a stored service whose container still runs is adopted and one whose container is gone has its serving revision relaunched in the background, reported as runtimeState RESTORING, then SERVING or UNAVAILABLE, by /browse/cloudrun and through the Ready and RoutesReady conditions. /run/invoke reaches the revision at the endpoint the gateway can reach and streams its response. These have component evidence only, against an in-memory Docker Engine double and Flyway PostgreSQL (CloudRunContainerSettingsTest, CloudRunTemplateFieldsTest, CloudRunStartupTest, CloudRunRestartTest, CloudRunInvokeTest); the CloudRunPlatformTest case that covers them is deferred and was not executed.

persistence.restartBehavior: Audited metadata survives restart while the LocalCloud volume is retained
recoveryLimitations: External runtime/data-plane side effects, if any, have separate lifecycle and recovery limits.

limitations: Workflow definitions and execution records persist. An execution that was ACTIVE when LocalCloud stopped is not resumed; it fails with InstanceRestart. An execution that was QUEUED has run no step and runs after the restart, from its first step, with the source and service account of the revision it was created for; it fails with InstanceRestart only when its workflow no longer exists. It is re-submitted once the gateway forwards the public port, so a first step that calls LocalCloud through localhost:5380 is served; if that signal is missing it runs 30 seconds after the backend start, with a warning in the log. In images up to 0.1.6 it could start a moment earlier and such a step got 503.

Connectors and expression/runtime behavior have bounded implementations and tests; complete Google connector/runtime parity remains unverified. A raised string is caught, passed to a retry predicate and raised again as the string, and a raised map as the map; reading e.code or e.message of a caught string is a TypeError; an execution ended by an uncaught raised string reports that string as its error, with error.payload as its JSON and no stackTrace. Known interpreter gaps are that an error with no type in Google's table of error tags carries the tag RuntimeError and LocalCloud's own code, such as NotFound, MissingArgument or StepLimitExceeded; connectors apply none of Google's built-in retry policies, raise no OperationError for a failed long-running operation, and report a target they cannot reach as an unclassified error without the ConnectionError, ConnectionFailedError or TimeoutError tag; the step limit is counted separately in each parallel branch, not once for the execution; and sys.get_env takes no default argument and provides none of Google's built-in variables, reading a name the workflow does not define from the LocalCloud process environment.

http.* calls raise HttpError for a 400 to 599 answer, ConnectionFailedError for a refused connection and TimeoutError for a timeout, as Google does; a workflow must catch the error instead of reading the response code. A connector's 4xx or 5xx answer is the same HttpError, with the numeric code, the response headers and the decoded body, so a handler reads e.code and e.body instead of the message text. Every error the interpreter raises carries tags. A subworkflow sees only its own parameters and variables, including workflow environment variables injected as implicit variables; use sys.get_env there, also in a parallel branch. Deployment rejects a parallel branch that assigns a parent variable not listed in shared, a return inside a parallel branch or iteration, a branches list outside 2 to 10, and an exception_policy other than continueAll. An execution may raise 100 unhandled errors in its parallel steps; the next one fails it with a ResourceLimitError that no except block catches, as the step limit does. sys.sleep rejects more than 31536000 seconds with ValueError.

events.await_callback returns the request, a map with http_request (body, headers, method, query and url), received_time and type, so the request body is http_request.body. An endpoint accepts the one method given as http_callback_method (POST by default) and answers 405 to any other. It keeps one request that arrives before the await and answers 429 to a second one until the first is taken; it can be awaited again and lives as long as its execution, after which it answers 404. The default timeout is 43200 seconds, and a timeout raises TimeoutError. Callback requests are not authorized, in any IAM mode; any caller that reaches the gateway is accepted, with no credential or with one that is not valid (WorkflowsCallbackAuthorizationComponentTest). The callback URL a workflow receives always names http://localhost:5380.

An execution runs as the workflow's serviceAccount, fixed when the execution is created; child executions use the child workflow's account. When serviceAccount is unset Google uses the Compute Engine default service account; LocalCloud uses the project's local default account (default@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com), which exists only for the gateway's configured project unless you create it.

http.* auth OIDC and OAuth2 sign as the execution account. Google allows these only for HTTPS endpoints; LocalCloud also signs for HTTP targets as a local development extension. A token that cannot be minted raises AuthError with IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE:<reason> and sends nothing; an unknown auth.type raises ValueError (local message text).

Cloud KMS and Cloud Storage connector calls are authorized as the workflow's service account through LocalCloud's internal caller identity (the Workflows service agent, not the local default account, when none is set). Other connector calls to LocalCloud carry an access token for the execution account; in open and permissive modes a connector call whose token cannot be minted is sent without credentials, while strict and gcp-live raise AuthError.

Creating a workflow with a serviceAccount, or an update that sets one, requires iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on that account in strict and gcp-live; open and permissive only log the decision. An unset serviceAccount is not checked, and LocalCloud's own seed and file-watcher deployments are not checked.

persistence.backingStore: PostgreSQL/MySQL data directories plus PostgreSQL metadata under /var/lib/localcloud
persistence.restartBehavior: Data survives restart with the LocalCloud volume when Cloud SQL is enabled
recoveryLimitations: Backups and managed recovery are not emulated.
Assembled image currently disables Cloud SQL despite registry default-on.

limitations: PostgreSQL and shared on-demand MySQL 8.4 data planes exist; MySQL logical schemas and wire users are isolated per project/instance, not separate servers.

Only PostgreSQL/MySQL databaseVersion identifiers are accepted. Version labels map to the installed shared engines; they do not provision a separate engine version per instance. settings.databaseFlags accepts the six flags that flags.list returns and answers 400 naming any other flag or a value outside its range. The PostgreSQL ones (default_transaction_isolation, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, lock_timeout, work_mem) are set on each database of the instance, so an already-open client session keeps its old value until it reconnects; the MySQL ones (character_set_server, collation_server) are the defaults of databases created afterwards, and the shared server's own variable does not change. Flags that need a server of their own, logging flags included, are refused. Tier, disk, IP, backup and maintenance settings remain descriptive metadata. PATCH preserves omitted settings; PUT without databaseFlags clears them.

Instance reads report ipAddresses from settings.ipConfiguration like Cloud SQL assigns them (PRIMARY unless ipv4Enabled is false, PRIVATE when privateNetwork is set); every address is 127.0.0.1, and the client uses the engine port (PostgreSQL 5391, MySQL 5406). IP settings and activationPolicy NEVER do not change where the data planes listen; a stopped instance stays RUNNABLE and keeps its addresses, as in Cloud SQL.

New databases apply native charset/collation and store native readback values. PostgreSQL encoding/collation cannot change in place; migrate data into a new database. MySQL ALTER DATABASE changes defaults, not existing column encodings. Older mismatched databases and missing user passwords require explicit repair or migration. New PostgreSQL clusters initialize with UTF8 encoding and C locale; existing clusters are preserved.

Required native work fails when the data plane is unavailable. Schema discovery returns per-database errors, shown in the Console. Creation reserves metadata before native provisioning and compensates newly created resources on failure.

With tls.enabled and the CA LocalCloud generates, serverCaCert on instances, connectSettings, listServerCas and sslCerts.insert is the CA the PostgreSQL and MySQL engines present, and sslCerts.insert and the ephemeral certificate endpoints issue a certificate signed by it for each request, so a driver can verify the server with the files the API returns. With operator-provided certificates LocalCloud has no CA key; it reports the last certificate of the chain and client certificates stay development material, as they do with TLS off. PostgreSQL asks for no client certificate, sslCerts.delete does not revoke, requireSsl and sslMode are not enforced, and resetSslConfig and the CA and server-certificate rotation verbs return DONE without doing work. Public certificate inventory is persisted in PostgreSQL and deleted with its instance. Component tests complete verify-ca and verify-full handshakes against PostgreSQL 17 and a certificate-required MySQL login; no image has run them.

Every operation the Cloud SQL Admin API returns is already DONE, because the work finishes before the request answers. No operation is ever PENDING or RUNNING and none carries an error; a failure is the HTTP error of the request itself, so code that polls an operation for an error never sees one.

instances.export, instances.import, instances.restoreBackup, instances.restart, promoteReplica, startReplica and stopReplica only check that the instance exists and return a DONE operation; they export, import, restore, restart or change nothing. Point-in-time restore returns a DONE operation without checking the source and creates no target instance.

An export, a project checkpoint and a migration capture hold a project's Cloud SQL instances, their databases and their user names, and data only for the tables of a PostgreSQL public schema; MySQL data, other PostgreSQL schemas and passwords are not in them. A reset would delete the instances with their data, so a checkpoint restore with replace and a runtime-migration run leave Cloud SQL as it is. The restore answers status partial_failure and names cloudsql under untouched_services; a migration run names it in its message. A restore without replace applies the section and runs its INSERT statements again.

MYSQL_* instances run in a companion Docker container that LocalCloud starts on first use, so they need the Docker socket; without it a request that needs the MySQL data plane fails with "Cloud SQL MySQL data plane requires Docker runtime access", while PostgreSQL instances keep working. Cloud SQL declares no Docker runtime dependency in localcloud.defaults.yaml, so its readiness entry does not report the missing socket.
backupRuns and backups are rows in PostgreSQL metadata and capture no database contents. preCheckMajorVersionUpgrade always returns an empty message list.
Local read-replica lifecycle and PSC configuration are software gaps. Real managed regional replication and Google PSC transport are production-only.

Microsoft Entra ID, SSRS leases, external physical sync, blue-green deployments, cross-region failovers, and online disk shrink are production-only enterprise/infrastructure capabilities excluded from local development.
